content: https://discord.com/channels/595666850260713488/892088344438255616/1549484532120428595 Responding here <@755590043632140352> (I do not have permission to respond in that channel 😅 ). Throughout the design discussions the request auth format updated from canonicalized URLs to opaque bytes. The spec advised that if unsupplied by the keymanager api, VCs should default to set their auth identical to the builder's URL. So no mention of http / https. A builder would want to check both or as implied by the existence of the opaque bytes, agree out-of-protocol on the specific bytes encoding (which could require https for example)

author: potuz
content: well, the point stands: if a builder actually checks against some string and doesn't want to verify twice or add a list of strings to match against, it should be very clear in the specifics of what the string must be, otherwise the response would probably be indistinguishable from "no bids here"
